summary: @lyxa.ai/core routes installer event bus and Redis traffic through author-controlled infrastructure via hardcoded credentials
details: The package's public `bootstrapCore` entrypoint unconditionally initializes the event bus against a hardcoded amqps:// URL embedding an author-owned CloudAMQP username and password (`amqps://adlvedna:<redacted>@dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com/adlvedna`). Any installer that calls `bootstrapCore` publishes event payloads to and consumes messages from this author-operated broker; consumed messages are dispatched into the installer's decorated handler methods. Separately, `ConfigurationService.redisURL` returns a value from a hardcoded `RedisUrlMap` keyed by environment (DEV/PREPROD/PROD), where each entry is an author-owned Redis Cloud URL with an embedded password (`redis://default:<redacted>@redis-*.redns.redis-cloud.com:*`). A caller-supplied `redisURL` option is discarded, so cache entries, BullMQ queues, and session-shape data written via RedisService go to the author's Redis instance, and reads from that instance can be influenced by anyone holding the shipped password. The tarball also embeds four Firebase Admin service-account JSON private keys for the author's Google projects (`for-poc-325210`, `lyxa-rider-88939`, `lyxa-shop`), plus the Redis and CloudAMQP passwords used above. The event-bus and Redis destinations are not documented caller-configurable endpoints; they are hardcoded in the main entry, and normal use of the advertised bootstrap API silently relays installer data to author-controlled infrastructure whose shared credentials are known to every downloader.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
